budget_items.what_was_said: The office reported four abatement requests and 43 motor vehicle excise tax abatements processed in Munis for September, awaiting payment processing by the tax collector.
FY2026 real estate exemption applications were mailed September 1st with an April 1 deadline; applications received by mid-November will still be applied to the next tax bill.
The 41D exemption amount was increased with a cost-of-living adjustment, and income/asset limits were adjusted at town meeting for both 41D and 17E/F.

budget_items.topic: Social security income deduction for 41D eligibility
budget_items.what_was_said: After consulting DLS, the assessor confirmed a social security income deduction can be applied to 41D applications, which brings some previously-excluded applicants back into eligibility.
Chapter land applications for fiscal year 2027 are due December 1st, and the office is now requiring all supporting paperwork before processing.

budget_items.topic: Roll-back tax invoice, 222 West Townsend Road
budget_items.what_was_said: A roll-back tax invoice was prepared after a chapter land property lost its exemption; the select board reportedly declined right of first refusal.
The FY2026 smart-growth cost report covering motor vehicle excise and additional property tax revenue, largely tied to Tri Town Drive, was submitted to DLS and the state; growth funding is expected.

New growth in tax dollars for residential, commercial, industrial and chapter land was reported, with personal property growth from a vendor still pending and expected to exceed the town's original estimate.

budget_items.topic: DLS request to accelerate free cash reporting
budget_items.what_was_said: The board noted a DLS request to accelerate free cash certification and said it needs to check with the town accountant on timing.
Discounts removed after inspections or non-response totaled a stated tax-assessed value and tax-dollar impact, following a Department of Revenue order to remove unexplained discounts.
A separate set of economic obsolescence discounts (excluding commercial items handled by the vendor) was removed, with a stated assessed-value and tax-dollar impact.
The board noted the 41A income limit had been unchanged for exactly two decades at a stated figure, which had caused at least one prior applicant to be rejected.

budget_items.topic: 41A adoption/interest rate proposal from Council on Aging
budget_items.what_was_said: A warrant article submitted via the Council on Aging proposed adopting 41A (already state-mandated and previously adopted) and lowering its interest rate; the assessor called it unnecessary and duplicative.

budget_items.topic: Roll-back taxes, chapter land release (six lots)
budget_items.what_was_said: A chapter land parcel is being released from chapter status, generating roll-back taxes with interest, with the property expected to become six new house lots.

budget_items.topic: GIS/mapping software ("One Map"/Data Scout) proposal cost
budget_items.what_was_said: A proposed GIS mapping and field-data platform was compared against the town's existing CI/CAI mapping contract, with a net annual cost increase discussed for switching or adding the new service.

Eight applications for a means-tested exemption were reported as qualifying, representing a small share of the tax levy, but there is no method in Munis to implement the burden-shift the statute requires.

budget_items.topic: Overlay account as possible funding source for means-tested exemptions
budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed whether the overlay reserve account could absorb the cost of the means-tested exemptions, noting that is not the account's intended purpose.
The board discussed wanting to increase the part-time inspector/assistant's hours, citing a backlog of roughly 500 needed inspections, ahead of the May town meeting.

decisions.decision: Assessor will apply the DLS-confirmed social security income deduction to 41D applications, restoring eligibility for some applicants close to the income limit.
Assessor asked the Town Manager's office to document the Select Board's declination of first refusal on 222 West Townsend Road in a letter for the file.
Board asked the assessor to have future sales reports sorted by percent change rather than by ratio, and broken out by neighborhood/site index.
Board agreed to hold off requesting a new sales report from the vendor until the Department of Revenue submission process is complete.
Revised 41A warrant article draft (with added income explanation) to be submitted to the Town Manager ahead of tomorrow's deadline.
No action needed on the Council on Aging's proposed 41A adoption/interest-rate warrant article, since 41A is already state-mandated and previously adopted; feedback given to the Town Manager.
Board will approve the eight qualifying means-tested exemption applications tonight contingent on later resolving how they will actually be funded/implemented in Munis.
Assessor will forward Westford's disabled-persons exemption criteria for the board to consider drafting a comparable local-option exemption.
Room reservation for the October 15th meeting will stand for now, to be cancelled if the date changes.

minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors reviewed routine assessing operations -- exemption and abatement processing, chapter land applications, removal of unsupported functional/economic obsolescence discounts, and pending vendor-supplied interim property valuations -- and worked through several minutes approvals. The most substantive discussion was that the town has no established mechanism to fund newly-authorized means-tested property tax exemptions, so the board planned to approve the current applicants contingent on resolving how the cost will be spread across taxpayers; the board also reviewed a GIS/mapping software proposal and discussed staffing and office-hours pressures. The meeting closed by entering executive session to discuss abatement/exemption applications under the statutory exemption for such proceedings.

what_happened.line: The board plans to approve eight qualifying means-tested property tax exemption applications, but only once it resolves how to actually fund and process them in the town's accounting system.
The assessor confirmed with the Department of Revenue that a social security income deduction can be applied to 41D applications, restoring eligibility for some applicants near the income limit.
The board asked the Town Manager's office to put in writing that the Select Board declined the town's right of first refusal on a property at 222 West Townsend Road.
A revised warrant article raising the 41A income limit, unchanged for two decades, is set to go to the Town Manager ahead of a filing deadline.
The meeting closed by moving into executive session to discuss pending abatement and exemption applications.

why_it_matters: Residents who applied for a means-tested tax exemption this cycle may see their exemption approved but delayed on the tax bill until the town settles how the cost is administered.
Seniors and other applicants near the income cutoff for the 41D deferral program may now qualify who previously did not, because of the confirmed income deduction.
A warrant article on the 41A deferral income limit is headed toward town meeting, which residents will eventually be asked to vote on.
watch_next: The board's next meeting, October 15, and whether the Munis funding mechanism for means-tested exemptions is resolved by then
The 41A warrant article submitted to the Town Manager

reconciliation.summary: The official minutes are a full, detailed record that agrees with ours on most figures and several decisions (the 41D social-security deduction amounts, FY2026 new growth, the 41A warrant timing, and the Council on Aging article being superfluous), but our minutes attach several dollar figures and topics (GIS/Data Scout costs, roll-back-tax lots, overlay-account amounts, staffing hours, economic-obsolescence figures) that appear nowhere in the official text, while the official record contains at least two agenda items — Master Plan Response and the Office Hours decision — and, most importantly, the actual approval of the eight means-tested exemption applications, that our minutes describe as decided but the official minutes never record as having happened. A person should specifically check whether the board actually voted to approve the eight means-tested exemption applications, since our minutes report that as a decision (t=5738) and the official minutes only discuss the unresolved MUNIS implementation problem with no approval recorded.
